status: Evidence-informed judgement. No study measures these effects for a fixed-price guaranteed-access system, so every value is an assumption that the cited evidence bounds.

a_household_food_waste_reduction_from_se.unit: fraction of baseline household food waste
a_household_food_waste_reduction_from_se.basis: UNEP FWI 2021/2024: household waste is similar across income groups (about 7 kg/cap/yr spread), so food security by itself does not cut waste. Inverted U (Lopez Barrera et al.): middle-income overbuying 'to avoid running out' is one waste channel that secure access could remove. WRAP 2020: waste FELL 34% (self-reported) under perceived insecurity, so the sign is ambiguous. Central 5% credits only the precautionary-overbuying channel. The high case also needs the absence of promotions and bulk discounts (assumption, not tested here).

b_precautionary_purchase_and_stockpiling.unit: fraction of shock-induced excess purchases (panic-buying spike volume) avoided
b_precautionary_purchase_and_stockpiling.steady_state_effect: negligible (no evidence of large standing household hoards in normal times)
b_precautionary_purchase_and_stockpiling.basis: Nielsen Ireland, week to 15 Mar 2020: grocery +23% y/y, toilet roll +181%, pasta +199%. The spike is scarcity-driven (Shah et al. 2012 mechanism). Damping needs a CREDIBLE guarantee plus regional catastrophe reserves (rule 13) and per-person purchase limits during shocks. The size of the damping is an assumption.

c_direct_rebound_energy_travel_fixed_pri.unit: fraction of efficiency-driven savings taken back as extra use
c_direct_rebound_energy_travel_fixed_pri.basis: Sorrell et al. 2009: household energy direct rebound 'generally less than 30%' (verified). Road transport 12% short run / 32% long run (OECD/ITF 2016, not verified). Fixed (non-zero) prices keep marginal cost and therefore limit rebound.

heat_flat_rate_billing_vs_metered_extra_.basis: Gibraltar/EED guidance: metering savings 'often reach 30%' (verified); other values search-only

public_transport_fare_free_trip_increase.basis: Tallinn +14% (verified), Dunkirk weekday +70% (verified); car substitution small (Luxembourg car commuting share 72.3% to 69.3% over 2011-2021)

c_direct_rebound_energy_travel_fixed_pri.design_rule: Keep energy and travel metered and priced per unit. Never use flat-rate or unlimited energy or travel.

d_goods_satiation_classification.evidence: India calories fell as incomes rose (Deaton & Dreze 2009); obesity link to insecurity only in HIC women (Nettle et al. 2017)
d_goods_satiation_classification.caveat: ultra-processed food raises intake by +508 kcal/day under free access (Hall 2019)

d_goods_satiation_classification.evidence: France: 2h15 (2011) to 3h03 (2015, +1.6% y/y) to 3h28 (2023); about 7 min/day
d_goods_satiation_classification.unira_effect: a one-off rise of about 35-55% to a ceiling, then flat
